mainTopic: Defining the items in the משנה that may not be sold to עובדי עבודה זרה: איצטרובלין, בנות שוח, פטוטרות, לבונה, and the exception for selling a large חבילה.
overview: The גמרא explains the hard words in the משנה's list of things you may not sell to an idol worshipper. איצטרובלין is first said to be תורניתא, but a ברייתא about שביעית rules that out, so רב ספרא and רבי אלעזר say it is cedar fruit. רבי יוחנן explains that בנות שוח are white figs and that פטוטרות means the fruits are forbidden only with their stems. ריש לקיש says לבונה means pure frankincense. A ברייתא allows selling any of these in a bundle of at least three מנים. אביי explains why possible resale is no concern: לפני עור only forbids helping the sinner directly. רבי יונה says a white rooster may be sold if the buyer just asks for 'a rooster.' The משנה seems to contradict him, and רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the משנה is about a buyer who points to 'this one and that one.' A ברייתא supports this, and a clash about a son's feast is answered as a casual party. Finally the גמרא begins asking what 'without specifying' and 'with specifying' mean in the משנה, and this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What is איצטרובלין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the משנה's word איצטרובלין means.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is איצטרובלין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה by asking what an unfamiliar word means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed איצטרובלין as something you may not sell to an idol worshipper. Before applying the rule, we need to know which plant this is.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
An item listed in the משנה; its identity is being clarified

phrases.english: Gemara: What is 'itzterubalin'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the item called איצטרובלין

steps.title: First answer: it is תורניתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא first identifies איצטרובלין as a plant called תורניתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is תורניתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer: איצטרובלין is a plant called תורניתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is only the opening suggestion. The next step will test it against a ברייתא and reject it.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of plant; the first suggested identity of איצטרובלין

phrases.english: Torenita.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 1

steps.title: A שביעית source contradicts the תורניתא answer
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא counts איצטרובלין among items that have שביעית rules, but a תורניתא has no עיקר, and things without an עיקר have no שביעית. So איצטרובלין cannot be תורניתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They contrasted it with a ברייתא: They added אלכסין, איצטרובלין, מוכססין and בנות שוח to the list. If you think איצטרובלין is תורניתא, does תורניתא have שביעית rules? But we learned: This is the rule: anything that has a root has שביעית, and anything that has no root has no שביעית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first answer. It brings a ברייתא that gives איצטרובלין the rules of שביעית, which does not fit a תורניתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only something that has an עיקר (a root) gets the rules of שביעית. The גמרא assumes a תורניתא counts as having no עיקר. So if the ברייתא gives איצטרובלין שביעית rules, it cannot be a תורניתא.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted it, pointing out a contradiction
The seventh year (שמיטה) and its rules for produce
A root, a lasting base in the ground

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא here is about שביעית, not עבודה זרה. The גמרא is only using it to find out what kind of plant איצטרובלין is.

phrases.english: And they contrasted it: They added to them
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the list of plants that have the rules of שביעית.

phrases.english: alekesin and itzterubalin, mukhsasin and benot shuach,
and if it enters your mind that itzterubalin is torenita,
is torenita subject to the Seventh Year?
But didn't we learn: 'This is the rule:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ עִיקָּר — יֵשׁ לוֹ שְׁבִיעִית,
phrases.english: anything that has a root is subject to the Seventh Year,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ עִיקָּר — אֵין לוֹ שְׁבִיעִית״!
phrases.english: and anything that has no root is not subject to the Seventh Year'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the identification given in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that איצטרובלין is תורניתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives איצטרובלין שביעית rules, but a תורניתא has no עיקר and so has no שביעית. The two cannot be the same thing.

steps.title: רב ספרא: it is the fruit of the cedar
steps.stepSummary: Dropping the first answer, רב ספרא says איצטרובלין is the fruit of the cedar tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב ספרא said: It is the fruit of the cedar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on תורניתא and offers a new identity: the fruit of a cedar tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cedar tree clearly has roots, so its fruit fits the ברייתא that gives איצטרובלין the rules of שביעית. The contradiction disappears.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Safra said:
the fruit of the cedar,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 2
steps.terutzMaskana: איצטרובלין is cedar fruit, which grows from a rooted tree and so has שביעית rules

steps.title: רבי אלעזר says the same
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports from ארץ ישראל that רבי אלעזר also identified איצטרובלין as cedar fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too, when רבין came, he said in the name of רבי אלעזר: the fruit of the cedar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב ספרא by showing that רבי אלעזר said the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new argument is added here. A second, independent voice agrees, which makes the cedar-fruit answer stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came from ארץ ישראל to בבל

steps.whatToRemember: איצטרובלין is not תורניתא. It is the fruit of the cedar, agreed on by רב ספרא and רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: And similarly, when Ravin came,
he said that Rabbi Elazar said:
the fruit of the cedar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 4 with a matching opinion
steps.raayaObject: רב ספרא's identification of איצטרובלין as cedar fruit

steps.title: בנות שוח are white figs
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the משנה's בנות שוח are white figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: בנות שוח: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: white figs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next word in the משנה and defines בנות שוח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple definition. בנות שוח is a kind of fig, a white fig.

phrases.english: Benot shuach:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
white figs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next term in the משנה

steps.title: פטוטרות means 'with their stems'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that פטוטרות is not another item; the משנה forbids the fruits when they are sold with their stems.
steps.simpleTranslation: And פטוטרות: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They taught this about the fruits with their stems.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the word פטוטרות in the משנה and says it describes how the fruits are sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פטוטרות is not a new kind of fruit. It tells us the ban applies when these fruits are sold still on their stems, not once the stems are removed.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read פטוטרות as one more forbidden item. It is a condition on the fruits already listed.

phrases.english: And petotarot:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
they taught it about the fruits with their stems.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the משנה's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fruits are forbidden only when sold with their stems

steps.title: לבונה means pure frankincense
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the משנה's לבונה means pure frankincense.
steps.simpleTranslation: Frankincense: רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: pure frankincense.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defines exactly which לבונה the משנה forbids selling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban is narrowed to pure frankincense, the kind used as incense for עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: Frankincense:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak said that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
pure frankincense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the משנה's list

steps.title: A large bundle may be sold
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that any of these items may be sold to them in a large bundle.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: And of all of them, one may sell them a bundle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives an exception to the whole list: selling in a big bundle is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who buys a large bundle is clearly buying to resell, not to offer to an idol. So the ban does not apply to large bundles.

keyTerms.meaning: A bundle, a large package of goods

phrases.english: It was taught: And of all of them,
one may sell to them a bundle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the משנה's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All the listed items may be sold to them in a large bundle

steps.title: How big is a bundle?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what size counts as a חבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is a bundle?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the minimum size of a חבילה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exception depends on the size of the bundle, so we need a clear measure.

phrases.english: And how much is a bundle?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the measure of the exception in step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum size of a חבילה

steps.title: At least three מנים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בתירא explains that a bundle is no less than three מנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן בתירא explained: A bundle is not less than three מנים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בן בתירא gives the minimum size of a חבילה: three מנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Below this weight it is not a bundle, so the normal ban stays in place. At three מנים or more, the sale is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure of one hundred דינרים

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's items (cedar fruit, white figs with stems, pure frankincense) may not be sold to an idol worshipper, except in a bundle of at least three מנים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira explained:
a bundle is not less than three maneh.
phrases.notes: A מנה is a hundred דינרים, so this means the weight of three hundred דינרים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A חבילה is at least three מנים (300 דינרים)

steps.title: What if the buyer resells it to someone who will offer it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why selling a large bundle is allowed, since the buyer may resell it to another non-Jew who will burn it as incense to an idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us worry that he will go and sell it to others, and they will burn it as an offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's rule that you may sell these items in a large bundle. Even if this buyer is not using it for an idol, maybe he will sell it to others who will.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The large bundle was allowed because a big amount is not bought for idol worship. The גמרא points out that this logic only covers the buyer himself. The bundle could still end up being used for עבודה זרה through a second person.

keyTerms.meaning: They burn it as an offering (incense)

phrases.english: But let us worry that perhaps he will go
phrases.notes: 'He' is the non-Jew who bought the large bundle from Step 9.

phrases.english: and sell it to others, and they will burn it as an offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the leniency of selling in a large bundle (Steps 9 and 11).
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא permitting sale in a large bundle
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even if the buyer will not offer it himself, resale to a worshipper should still be a concern.

steps.title: אביי: we are only commanded about the direct sinner
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the prohibition of לפני עור only forbids directly helping the sinner, not helping someone who might later help him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We are commanded about 'before' (the blind). We are not commanded about 'before' someone who is 'before' (the blind).
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the ברייתא. The Torah only forbids handing the stumbling block straight to the person who will sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issur of לפני עור לא תתן מכשול covers being the direct cause of someone's sin. Selling to a middleman who might resell to a worshipper is one step removed, so it is not included. That is why the large bundle stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Before', the word from the פסוק 'לפני עור לא תתן מכשול' (ויקרא 19:14)
'Before the before', one step removed from the sinner

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a limit on לפני עור. Indirect help, through a middleman, does not fall under this specific issur.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
We are commanded about 'before',
phrases.notes: This is the word 'before' in 'Do not place a stumbling block before the blind' (ויקרא 19:14).

phrases.english: we are not commanded about 'before' someone who is 'before'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַ״לִּפְנֵי״ מִפַּקְּדִינַן, אַ״לִּפְנֵי״ דְּ״לִפְנֵי״ לָא מִפַּקְּדִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the resale challenge of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any sale that could eventually lead to idol worship should be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: לפני עור only forbids directly enabling the sinner, so possible resale is not a concern.

steps.title: רבי יונה: what the non-Jew asks for decides it
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's white rooster, רבי יונה rules that if the non-Jew asks for 'a rooster' you may sell him a white one, but if he asks for 'a white rooster' you may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'and a white rooster.' רבי יונה said in the name of רבי זירא in the name of רב זביד (and some teach it as רבי יונה in the name of רבי זירא alone): If he says 'Who has a rooster?', it is permitted to sell him a white rooster. If he says 'Who has a white rooster?', it is forbidden to sell him a white rooster.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next item in the משנה, the white rooster. רבי יונה explains when the issur applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A white rooster was a typical idol offering. If the non-Jew asks specifically for a white one, that shows he wants it for the idol, so selling is forbidden. If he just asks for any rooster, there is no sign of idol worship, so even a white one may be sold.

keyTerms.meaning: And some teach it (in a different way)

phrases.english: And a white rooster.
phrases.notes: These are words quoted from the משנה, which lists a white rooster among the things you may not sell.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָה אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב זְבִיד,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yona said in the name of Rabbi Zeira in the name of Rav Zevid,
and some teach it this way:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָה אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yona said in the name of Rabbi Zeira:
If he says 'Who has a rooster?'
it is permitted to sell him a white rooster;
if he says 'Who has a white rooster?'
it is forbidden to sell him a white rooster.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַרְנְגוֹל לָבָן. אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָה אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from frankincense and bundles to the next item in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A white rooster is forbidden only when the non-Jew asks specifically for a white rooster.

steps.title: Quoting רבי יהודה from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה in the משנה, who allows selling a white rooster mixed in with other roosters, to set up a challenge to רבי יונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: רבי יהודה says, he may sell him a white rooster among the roosters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge against רבי יונה. It quotes רבי יהודה's ruling and will now analyze it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה permits a white rooster only when it is sold together with other roosters. This implies the תנא קמא forbids it even then. The גמרא will use this to test רבי יונה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Among the roosters, mixed in with other roosters

phrases.english: We learned: Rabbi Yehuda says:
He may sell him a white rooster
among the roosters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה source to test רבי יונה's ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only; the conflict comes out in Steps 16 to 18.

steps.title: What case is רבי יהודה talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exact situation the משנה is describing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the non-Jew said in the משנה's case. This sets up the next two moves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יונה made everything depend on what the non-Jew asked for. So the גמרא needs to know what he asked for in the משנה's case before it can compare.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?

phrases.english: What is the case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what case the quoted משנה refers to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the non-Jew in the משנה asked for 'a rooster' or for 'a white rooster'.

steps.title: It cannot be when he asked for a white rooster
steps.stepSummary: If the non-Jew asked for a white rooster, even selling it among other roosters would be forbidden, so that cannot be רבי יהודה's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he said 'Who has a white rooster, who has a white rooster?', then even among the roosters it should also not be allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first option and rejects it. If he asked for a white one, mixing it with others does not help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the non-Jew has said he wants a white rooster, his idol-worship purpose is clear, and hiding it among other roosters changes nothing. Since רבי יהודה does allow it among the roosters, his case must be different.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, if we suggest

phrases.english: If you say that he said:
'Who has a white rooster, who has a white rooster?'
then even among the roosters it should also not be allowed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to Step 16 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The option that the משנה is a case where he asked for a white rooster
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In that case mixing with other roosters could not make it permitted, yet רבי יהודה permits it.

steps.title: So the תנא קמא forbids it even when he only asked for 'a rooster'
steps.stepSummary: The case must be where he asked for just 'a rooster.' Even so רבי יהודה only allows it among other roosters, which means the תנא קמא forbids it completely. That contradicts רבי יונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not that he said 'Who has a rooster, who has a rooster?' And even so, according to רבי יהודה, among the roosters, yes; by itself, no. And according to the תנא קמא, even among the roosters it is also not allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge. Even when the non-Jew only asks for 'a rooster,' the משנה still treats a white rooster as a problem, which goes against רבי יונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יונה said asking for 'a rooster' makes a white one fully permitted. But in the משנה, in that exact case, רבי יהודה still forbids a white rooster sold by itself, and the תנא קמא forbids it even mixed with others. So neither opinion matches רבי יונה.

keyTerms.meaning: The first (unnamed) opinion in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is the lenient one here, but even he does not fully agree with רבי יונה. The challenge comes mainly from the תנא קמא, who is stricter still.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יונה: asking for 'a rooster' lets you sell a white one. The משנה seems to say that even then a white rooster is restricted. The next step answers this challenge.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that he said:
'Who has a rooster, who has a rooster?'
And even so, according to Rabbi Yehuda,
among the roosters, yes;
by itself, no;
and according to the first tanna,
phrases.notes: He is the unnamed first opinion in the משנה, the one who forbids selling a white rooster.

phrases.english: even among the roosters it is also not allowed!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו דְּקָא אָמַר ״תַּרְנְגוֹל לְמִי, תַּרְנְגוֹל לְמִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the first option in Step 17, it settles on the second option and draws the contradiction with רבי יונה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יונה's ruling that asking for 'a rooster' permits selling a white one
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the case where he asked for just 'a rooster,' the משנה still restricts a white rooster: the תנא קמא completely, and רבי יהודה unless it is mixed with others.

steps.title: The case is a buyer who points to several roosters
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that the משנה is talking about a buyer who points and says 'this one and that one,' and one of them is white.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The משנה is talking about a buyer who points to roosters and says 'this one and that one.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge against רבי יונה by giving the משנה a new case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 assumed the משנה meant a buyer who just asked for 'a rooster,' which made the תנא קמא contradict רבי יונה. רב נחמן בר יצחק says the משנה means a buyer who points at specific birds. So a plain request for 'a rooster' stays permitted for everyone, and רבי יונה is safe.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what case are we dealing with? (introduces a narrower reading)
This one and that one: the buyer points to specific birds

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Here, what are we dealing with?
For example, where he said "this one and that one."
phrases.notes: He points at a few roosters, and one of the ones he picked happens to be white.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 by changing which case the משנה describes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about a buyer who asked for just 'a rooster,' so the תנא קמא forbids even that.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a buyer who points to specific birds. Asking for 'a rooster' is permitted to everyone, as רבי יונה said.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the 'this one and that one' reading
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה: it is forbidden only if the buyer says 'this white rooster.' It is permitted if he says 'this one and that one,' and even 'this rooster' is permitted when he is making a feast for his son or has a sick person at home.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is also taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה said, When is it forbidden? When he said 'this white rooster.' But if he said 'this one and that one,' it is permitted. And even if he said 'this rooster,' if the non-Jew is making a feast for his son or has a sick person in his house, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא openly mentions the 'this one and that one' case, which is exactly how רב נחמן בר יצחק explained the משנה. It also adds a new point: when there is a clear non-idol reason for wanting the rooster, like a son's feast or a sick person, selling is allowed even if he pointed to a white one.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way: a ברייתא supports what was just said
A white rooster, the kind used in idol worship

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
Rabbi Yehuda said: When (is it forbidden)?
When he said, "this white rooster,"
But if he said "this one and that one" — it is permitted.
And even if he said "this rooster,"
a non-Jew who made a feast for his son

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ חוֹלֶה בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: or who had a sick person in his house — it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 19 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading that the משנה is about 'this one and that one.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in the name of רבי יהודה that names the 'this one and that one' case.

steps.title: Another teaching forbids dealing with him on the day of his son's feast
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from a teaching that forbids business with a non-Jew on the day of his son's feast.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught: A non-Jew who made a feast for his son, it is forbidden only on that day and only with that man. So at least on that day and with that man it IS forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last part of the ברייתא, which allowed selling during a son's feast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that a son's feast is a reason to permit the sale. But another teaching says a son's feast is exactly when dealing with that non-Jew is forbidden, because idol worship is part of that celebration. The two teachings seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: That day and that man: the limits of the restriction

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
A non-Jew who made a feast for his son,
it is forbidden only on that day
and only with that man.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם וְאוֹתוֹ הָאִישׁ מִיהָא אָסוּר!
phrases.english: That day and that man, at least, are forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the feast clause of the ברייתא brought in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that a son's feast makes it permitted to sell a rooster.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another teaching treats the son's feast day as a time when dealing with that non-Jew is forbidden, so the feast cannot be a reason to permit.

steps.title: The ברייתא means a casual party
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר רב משרשיא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a casual party, not the big feast meant by the other teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר רב משרשיא said: It is talking about a casual party (טווזיג).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying the two teachings talk about two different kinds of party.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidden 'feast for his son' is a major celebration, where idol worship is part of the event. The ברייתא that permits selling is about a casual get-together, where no idol worship is involved. So the two teachings do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: A casual social party, not a major celebration

steps.whatToRemember: A white rooster may be sold when the buyer just asks for 'a rooster,' when he points to 'this one and that one,' or when he clearly needs it for a casual party or a sick person. It is forbidden when he asks for 'this white rooster.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzḥak bar Rav Mesharshiya said:
It is talking about a casual party.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא: בְּטַוְוזִיג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both teachings talk about the same feast, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: The forbidding teaching is about a major feast; the permitting ברייתא is about a casual party.

steps.title: What do 'without specifying' and 'with specifying' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about 'all other items' and asks what 'without specifying' and 'with specifying' mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: And all other items, without specifying it is permitted, and with specifying it is forbidden. What is 'without specifying' and what is 'with specifying'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks what its two key words mean. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that other items are permitted to sell when the buyer does not specify, and forbidden when he does. The גמרא wants to know exactly what kind of 'specifying' the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: When the buyer does not specify

phrases.english: We learned (in the משנה):
And all the other items —
without specifying, it is permitted; with specifying, it is forbidden.
What is "without specifying" and what is "with specifying"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact meaning of 'without specifying' and 'with specifying' in the משנה.

steps.title: A first suggestion: 'white wheat' versus 'for idol worship'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that 'without specifying' means he asks for white wheat, and 'with specifying' means he says it is for idol worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say: 'without specifying' is where he says 'white wheat,' and 'with specifying' is where he says 'for idol worship.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first possible answer, using the word 'אילימא,' which signals that it is about to be challenged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this suggestion, asking for 'white wheat' (without saying why) is permitted, and saying 'for idol worship' is forbidden. But it would be obvious that selling something openly for idol worship is forbidden, so the גמרא is setting up a question about why the משנה would need to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say: introduces a suggestion that will be challenged

steps.confusionAlert: 'אילימא' is not the final answer. It is a suggestion the גמרא brings up in order to knock it down.

phrases.english: If you say:
"without specifying" is where he says "white wheat,"
"with specifying" is where he says "for idol worship."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question of step 23, setting up a challenge.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A tentative answer: unspecified means asking for 'white wheat'; specified means saying it is for idol worship.
